content.title: Watch Artemis 2 launch from NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida
content.text: Updated April 1, 2026, 5:08 p.m. MTFour astronauts, including one pilot who completed flight training in Texas, will soon embark on a mission to the moon.The Artemis II mission is expected to take off from NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida at 4:24 p.m. MT/5:24 p.m. CT on Wednesday, April 1, carrying four astronauts away from the Earth and towards the moon on a spacecraft called Orion. The crew will work with scientists back on Earth to "facilitate science investigations to inform future human spaceflight missions."The crew includes Victor Glover, a pilot who completed his advanced flight training in Kingsville, Texas and earned his wings of gold on December 14, 2001. Glover is a California native, but some of his family, including his father, live in Prosper, Texas (the Dallas-Fort Worth area).Glover is also making history as the first Black man to venture near the moon.The crew also consists of Commander Reid Wiseman and mission specialists Christina Koch and Jeremy Hansen. Koch will be the first woman to venture near the moon, while Hanson is the first Canadian to venture near the moon.While Artemis II will not land on the moon, it will pick up where the 1972 Apollo 17 mission left off and set the stage for the upcoming Artemis III test flight in 2027, the Artemis IV landing in 2028, and NASA's plans to establish a lunar base.Here's how to watch the launch. Sen. Ted Cruz said he worked to 'advance the success' of Artemis IIIn an X post prior to the launch, U.S. Sen. Ted Cruz said that, as Chairman of the Senate Commerce Committee, he worked to advance the Artemis II program."...I’ve worked to advance the success of the Artemis II program by advancing the NASA reauthorization bill last month, empowering NASA to help return American astronauts to the Moon and carry out the President’s National Space Policy.," Cruz said on X. Are there people on Artemis 2?Yes, the crew consists of Commander Reid Wiseman, Pilot Victor Glover, and Mission Specialists Christina Koch and Jeremy Hansen. Artemis 2 launches from FloridaThe Artemis II mission launched from NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida at 4:35 MT/5:35 CT on Wednesday, April 1, carrying four astronauts away from the Earth and towards the moon on a spacecraft called Orion. When will Artemis 2 reach the moon?The crew will have to travel some 244,000 miles (393,000 kilometers) away to reach the moon, which will take several days.Watch Artemis II rocket launch today; live countdownYou can watch the USA TODAY livestream and follow along with a live countdown below. When was the last time we went to the moon?The last humans to visit the moon happened on December 19, 1972, when Apollo 17 astronauts splashed down in the Pacific. They were the last humans to visit the moon—and the last to be more than 400 miles from the Earth. Since that date, astronauts have only been in low Earth orbit, according to the National Air and Space Museum. How tall is Artemis 2 moon rocket?The Space Launch System stands at 322 feet tall when fully stacked, making it one of NASA's largest rockets ever. Artemis 2 launch locationNASA's Artemis missions will launch from Kennedy Space Center in Cape Canaveral, on Florida's Atlantic coast. Jeremy HansenCanadian Jeremy Hansen, 50, is the only Artemis II crew member who will be making his first voyage to space. Artemis 3 launch dateArtemis III, scheduled for 2027, will fly in low Earth orbit and test one or both of the commercial landers from SpaceX and Blue Origin.Artemis II launch time CSTMost of the Lone Star State is in the Central Time Zone. Most Texans can catch the launch starting at 5:24 p.m. CT on Wednesday, April 1.You can also watch livestreams on Amazon Prime, NASA's YouTube channel, and NASA+.Who are the astronauts on Artemis 2?The crew consists of Commander Reid Wiseman, Pilot Victor Glover, and Mission Specialists Christina Koch and Jeremy Hansen.Three of the four astronauts on the Artemis II mission are setting records:First woman to venture near the moon: Mission Specialist Christina KochFirst Black man to venture near the moon: pilot Victor GloverFirst Canadian to venture near the moon: Mission Specialist Jeremy HansenWhere will Artemis 2 launch from?The Artemis II mission is launching from NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida.Where is Artemis 2 going?The mission will send astronauts on a 10-day journey around the moon and back. While no landing is in store for the astronauts, the mission serves as a vital test flight to lay the groundwork for humans to make it back to the surface in as little as two years.Along the way, the Artemis II astronauts will make history, venturing about 250,000 miles in space – further than the record-setting Apollo 13 mission – while seeing sights of the far side of the moon that no human has ever laid eyes upon.Will Artemis 2 land on the moon?While Artemis II will not be landing on the moon, it is a step towards NASA's plans to set up a lunar base.When does the Artemis 2 launch?The Artemis II mission is expected to take off from NASA’s Kennedy Space Center in Florida at 4:24 p.m. MT/5:24 p.m. CT on Wednesday, April 1,What is the Artemis 2 mission?Under its Artemis campaign, NASA is aiming to return astronauts to the surface of the moon for the first time since the Apollo missions came to an end in 1972.But this time, astronauts won't simply plant the stars and stripes before heading back to Earth. NASA is looking to establish a permanent foothold on the lunar south pole, using a series of crewed and uncrewed missions in the years ahead to build a moon base.From there, the first humans could be venturing to Mars.How long will Artemis 2 take to get to the moon?The crew will spend several days traveling to the moon, according to NASA.USA TODAY contributed to this story.Natassia Paloma may be reached at npaloma@gannett.com, @NatassiaPaloma on x; natassia_paloma on Instagram, and Natassia Paloma Thompson on Facebook.
